title: Completed exchange coherence
statement:
Completed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] is
natural in $K$, equals the identity for identity squares, and satisfies
horizontal and vertical pasting after the canonical associativity
isomorphisms.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states these coherence properties of
the completed exchange: Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) asserts only that the
base-change map is an isomorphism, Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)) gives the functoriality of
$Lf^*_{comp}$ and of $Rf_*$ alone, and the nearest recorded coherence of the
two ingredients is the commutativity of the projection formula with the base
change map, Remark 21.50.2 ([Tag
0E48](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E48)), stated for a single
square of ringed topoi without coefficients or completion. The blueprint
adds naturality in $K$, the identity-square statement and horizontal and
vertical pasting for the completed exchange.

proof.text: Unfold [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map]. For each square write $S_\square=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K$ and $T_\square=Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$, and retain exactly its maps $s_\square:S_\square\simeq\Rlim B_\bullet$ and $c_\square:T_\square\simeq\Rlim D_\bullet$. Then $\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_\square=c_\square^{-1}\circ\Rlim(v'_\bullet)\circ s_\square$. Restrict to constant $A$ coefficients using [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; this is an equivalence on derived-complete objects and identifies derived limits, quotient towers and completion units. Thus it reflects the equations to be proved, without identifying the two ambient module categories.

source.place: Proof, passage to reconstruction comparisons; Detailed form Proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization] to identify the specified $v'_\bullet$ with $E^{\mathcal T}_\square$, the mate of the constant-coefficient pullback square, as an actual morphism in the derived category of strict towers. This replaces the invalid direct application of the bounded-below abelian etale laws to pro-etale module towers. The reduction statement [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-map-reduction] checks the resulting finite components and their transition compatibility; it is not used to infer equality of tower morphisms from equality of their derived evaluations.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences; strict tower normalization of the finite maps

proof.text:
The constant-coefficient pullback composition maps are termwise maps of strict tower complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] they are the canonical module pullback compositions; associativity is checked before localization: both iterated inverse-image section maps are pullback along the same composite, and the coefficient balancing maps send $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes abc$. Units send $x\otimes1$ to $x$. Hence the two pasted pullback squares agree with the outer square on complexes of towers and therefore in their localization. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (4) for identity, (1) for horizontal pasting, and (2), followed by (3), for vertical pasting. In coordinates in which pullback and direct-image composition comparisons are suppressed, the equations in $D(\mathcal T)$ are
$$E^{\mathcal T}_{\mathrm{id}}=1,\quad E^{\mathcal T}_{21}=(E^{\mathcal T}_2G_{g'})\circ(G_hE^{\mathcal T}_1),\quad E^{\mathcal T}_{13}=(R_{f'}^{\mathcal T}E^{\mathcal T}_3)\circ(E^{\mathcal T}_1R_e^{\mathcal T}).$$
For the horizontal squares use $(f,f',g,g')$ and $(f',f'',h,h')$; for the vertical squares use $(f,f',g,g')$ and $(e,e',g',g'')$. The direct-image composition maps in the last formula are the conjugates of the pullback composition maps, as prescribed by mate-pasting (3). Since $E^{\mathcal T}$ is a natural transformation, its naturality equation holds for every morphism of the input tower, not merely endomorphisms.

source.place: Proof, finite-level S0/S8 equations, realized in the strict tower derived categories

proof.text: Use the functor $\Rlim$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] on the preceding tower equalities. It preserves identities and composites, so if $U:V_0\to V_1$ and $V:V_1\to V_2$ are the two tower arrows in either pasting formula, then $\Rlim(VU)=\Rlim(V)\Rlim(U)$. Every compatible tower comparison used to change coordinates is invertible after $\Rlim$ by [lemma-weil-pbc-r-lim-levelwise-isomorphism]. This uses equality in the derived tower category established in step 3; componentwise equality alone would not suffice.

source.place: Proof, third sentence: apply Rlim to tower equations

proof.text: Identify the intermediate completed expressions with the limits of the intermediate towers. For completed pullbacks use the canonical reduction comparisons of [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] and the strict pullback construction of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]; its normalization sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes q(b)a$, so successive quotient identifications and their unit identifications agree. For direct images use the functorial projection-formula and direct-image/limit comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Their composition compatibility can be checked on the defining limit of a K-injective tower: both iterated direct-image/limit maps have $n$-th projection the direct image of the same tower projection, hence are the same map by the universal property of that limit [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]. These right adjoints preserve K-injective complexes because their constant-coefficient inverse images are exact [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], so this calculation descends to the specified derived comparisons. The projection-formula comparisons identify the reduction of a direct image with the direct image reduction, and their maps are functorial and quotient-compatible by [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Consequently in a pasted diagram the target comparison of the first arrow and the source comparison of the second are the same intermediate comparison, with the canonical pullback and direct-image associativity maps retained. The calculation is on strict models and their canonical comparisons, not uniqueness of a map between abstract Roos triangles. For the horizontal compatibility involving the projection maps, apply the Cartesian-square rectangle of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-base-change-naturality] with $Q=P_n$: its two routes are precisely $v'_nh_n$ and $h'_nv_n$. For vertical composition, the projection map of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is the adjunct of the tensor comparison followed by the counit. Under the composite pullback adjunction, the transpose of either successive projection maps or the composite projection map is $(\varepsilon_e\circ L_e\varepsilon_fR_e)\otimes1$, after the canonical tensor associativity maps. This is the composite counit specified in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (2); injectivity of adjunction transposition makes those projection maps equal. These identities use the canonical module/tensor comparisons in constant-coefficient coordinates from step 1; they do not assume $u^{-1}A_T\to A_{T'}$ is an isomorphism for completed coefficient sheaves. Thus projection maps, as well as limit comparisons, respect the pasting coordinates.

source.place: Proof, reconstruction/projection/direct-image comparisons; argument expanding the conjugation sentence

proof.text:
Write $a_i:C_i\simeq\Rlim V_i$ for the specified comparisons at the three vertices of either pasted route, including the associativity maps just checked. Its two completed arrows are $a_1^{-1}\Rlim(U)a_0$ and $a_2^{-1}\Rlim(V)a_1$ by the ordered composite of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], the normalization in step 2 and the intermediate comparisons in step 5. Their composite is
$$a_2^{-1}\Rlim(V)a_1a_1^{-1}\Rlim(U)a_0=a_2^{-1}\Rlim(VU)a_0.$$
By steps 3 and 4 this is the outer completed exchange, proving both horizontal and vertical pasting. For an identity square the source and target comparisons coincide by their unit normalizations in step 5, so $a^{-1}\Rlim(1)a=1$. No choice of arbitrary isomorphisms is made.

source.place: Proof, final conjugation sentence: explicit pasting and identity cancellation

proof.text:
For a morphism $k:K\to H$, write $u:S_K\to S_H$ and $w:T_K\to T_H$ for its source and target functor images. Naturality of the comparisons in step 5 gives $a_{0,H}u=\Rlim(u_\bullet)a_{0,K}$ and $a_{1,H}w=\Rlim(w_\bullet)a_{1,K}$. Naturality of the tower mate in step 3 gives $w_\bullet E_K=E_Hu_\bullet$. Substitution into the defining composite gives
$$w\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_K=a_{1,H}^{-1}\Rlim(w_\bullet E_K)a_{0,K}=a_{1,H}^{-1}\Rlim(E_Hu_\bullet)a_{0,K}=\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_H u.$$
This proves naturality for arbitrary morphisms. Restriction of scalars reflects all these equations by the equivalence in step 1.

source.place: Proof, naturality in K and final reconstruction

blueprint_sketch.statement:
The completed exchange map is natural in $K$, is the identity for identity
squares, and commutes with horizontal and vertical pasting.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
At every finite level these equations are the S0/S8 equations. They commute
with the tower transitions by naturality of coefficient reduction. Apply
$R\varprojlim$ to each equality and conjugate by the same reconstruction,
projection-formula, and direct-image/limit isomorphisms used in the definition.
The resulting equations are precisely the completed equations.

split_report.summary: Second reading repaired the coefficient-category mismatch and the unsupported inference from finite component equations to derived tower equations. One smaller unsplit node identifies the specified strict tower exchange with its adjunction mate. Seven steps apply the existing generic mate-pasting laws in the derived strict-tower categories, apply the cited Rlim functor, check canonical intermediate comparisons, and write identity, pasting and arbitrary-morphism naturality cancellations explicitly.
split_report.blueprint: Proof, first two sentences: strict tower mate normalization and S0/S8 equations; third sentence: the Rlim functor; final sentence: canonical reconstruction comparisons and explicit cancellation. Detailed form Proof realized without assuming derived evaluations are faithful.
